summary: WorldEntity duplicate diagnostics are bounded by entry count but not by retained string bytes, so rejected duplicates can pin arbitrarily large kind/recipeKey payloads.
evidence: Current WorldEntity hardening PR #293 head 91b6e273c0c21326dfbfe9c5ee5227e99f26933e bounds persistentState depth, nodes, and string bytes, but checkedNonEmpty still imposes no byte ceiling on WorldEntity.kind or origin.worldId/regionId/generator/recipeKey.

createRegistry stores up to duplicateDiagnosticCapacity diagnostics (default 64); each rejected duplicate diagnostic retains incomingKind and incomingRecipeKey directly, so element-count boundedness does not bound retained bytes.

A caller can repeatedly submit duplicate records with the same valid id and very large metatable-free kind/recipeKey strings. The records are rejected for identity collision but their strings remain reachable through the diagnostics ring until eviction, creating a bounded-count/unbounded-memory path outside MAX_PERSISTENT_STATE_STRING_BYTES.

The deterministic core already uses 512-byte ceilings for semantic parts/scopes, demonstrating an existing project convention for bounding canonical semantic strings; the WorldEntity metadata boundary currently has no analogous limit.

metadata.recommendedAction: Add explicit byte ceilings or an aggregate canonical-metadata byte budget before ownership/diagnostic retention, with boundary tests for accepted maximums and rejected oversize duplicate kind/recipeKey strings. Keep the change separate from persistentState budgeting if #293 is already integration-bound.
